newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan insurers to refocus under Big Bang.
newsitem.headline: Japan insurers to refocus under Big Bang.

text.p: The new chief of Japan's life insurance body says that he does not expect the country's sweeping "Big Bang" financial reforms to lead to a shake-up in the industry.

Yuzuru Fujita, the chairman of the Life Insurance Association of Japan, said that, instead, deregulation will force life insurers to improve their financial health and strengthen their areas of expertise.
"I don't expect an industry-wide restructuring any time soon," Fujita told Reuters in a recent interview.
"In the first round, life insurers will take a closer look at their operations and withdraw from unprofitable business areas and strengthen already strong areas," he said.
After that, some insurers may seek to merge or acquire other firms to deal with the competition, he said.

In June, Japan unveiled a blueprint for Big Bang reforms that will break down barriers between the banking, securities and insurance sectors. The securities sector faces sweeping changes in the coming few years, but the pace of reforms in the insurance industry will be relatively moderate.
For instance, banks are expected to be allowed to enter the insurance market through their subsidiaries by the end of 2001.
Analysts said that allowing financially strong banks to enter the insurance sector was one of the toughest issues to resolve as life insurance companies feared that they would lose business to banks.
But the insurers agreed to a compromise whereby banks would not be allowed to sell insurance policies through their vast branch networks.
Banks' securities subsidiaries are currently allowed to engage in the securities business in a limited form but that will change under the Big Bang reforms.
Insurance companies will also be allowed to set up holding companies for financial services after steps are taken to protect policyholders and to improve the financial health of insurance companies.
Fujita, the president of Asahi Mutual Life Insurance Co, assumed the post of chairman of the industry group last month. The body groups 44 Japanese life insurers.
He said that the industry wants the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to work out an insurance payment guarantee system as soon as possible in order to restore confidence in the industry.
The system would be used to protect policyholders in case insurance companies face financial difficulties.

The operating environment for life insurers has become tougher in recent months, following the business failure of Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, which increased concern about the health of Japanese life insurers.
MOF suspended part of Nissan Mutual's business on April 25, marking the first failure of a life insurance firm in post-war Japan.

"To protect policyholders, we need two measures -- implementing something like the prompt corrective action (PCA) system to prevent the failure of an insurer and the payment guarantee system to ensure payment of policyholders' contracts." "We think the two measures will be introduced together as soon as possible," he said.
A PCA system would gauge the health of insurers, similar to one the banking industry currently employs.
